% Drawn here rather than with pdfpages' own frame option, which is a
% black hairline with no way to soften it. Matched to the book's hairline
% gray: a third of a point at 3.95:1, which a laser prints faithfully and
% which is still light enough that a remnant of it after an imperfect cut
% does not read as a border. The first attempt at 9A9A9A looked right on
% screen and needed good light to follow on paper.
\definecolor{cutline}{HTML}{7E7E7E}
\newcommand{\cutlines}{%
  \begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture, overlay]
    \draw[cutline, line width=0.3pt] ([xshift=16.1mm]current page.north west) -- ([xshift=16.1mm]current page.south west);
    \draw[cutline, line width=0.3pt] ([xshift=105mm]current page.north west) -- ([xshift=105mm]current page.south west);
    \draw[cutline, line width=0.3pt] ([xshift=193.9mm]current page.north west) -- ([xshift=193.9mm]current page.south west);
    \draw[cutline, line width=0.3pt] ([yshift=-8.8mm]current page.north west) -- ([yshift=-8.8mm]current page.north east);
    \draw[cutline, line width=0.3pt] ([yshift=-148.5mm]current page.north west) -- ([yshift=-148.5mm]current page.north east);
    \draw[cutline, line width=0.3pt] ([yshift=-288.2mm]current page.north west) -- ([yshift=-288.2mm]current page.north east);
  \end{tikzpicture}}
\AddToHook{shipout/background}{\cutlines}
